question: I'm porting an EVM/Solidity contract to Soroban: how do ERC-20 and ERC-3643-style tokens, `msg.sender`, `address(0)`, gas, and view calls map, is there a Solidity compiler, and what is the biggest footgun?

golden.answer: Port the design, not Solidity inheritance. ERC-20 maps to the Stellar Asset Contract or a SEP-41 token; ERC-3643-style regulated tokens can use Draft SEP-57, and ERC-1404 and ERC-1410 have no one-to-one standard. There is no ambient `msg.sender`: pass an `Address` and call `require_auth`; mis-scoped auth is the main footgun. There is no null address: use `Option<Address>` or explicit state. Gas becomes multidimensional resource fees (CPU, memory, ledger I/O, size, rent), and simulation discards writes. Solang's Soroban target is pre-alpha; Rust with the Soroban SDK is the default.
keyFacts: No ambient `msg.sender`: pass an `Address`, call `require_auth`; auth is the main footgun.
ERC-20 maps to SAC or SEP-41; ERC-3643-style controls can use Draft SEP-57.
No null address: use `Option<Address>` or explicit state, never an all-zero address.
Solang's Soroban target is pre-alpha; Rust with the Soroban SDK is the default route.
avoid: Do NOT claim that SEP-57 is Final, or automatically covers ERC-1404 and ERC-1410.
Do NOT claim that Solang's Soroban target is production-ready.
golden.notes: Grade the Draft and pre-alpha statuses, not release numbers (SEP-57 v0.4.0 and Solang 0.4.0 as of 2026-11-14). Auth, not syntax, is the top footgun.

Solang repository was live and active on 2026-06-29; answer still treats Rust/Soroban SDK as the default production route.
Also good if the answer: Warns that there is no universal zero/null address pattern; use explicit `Option`, sentinel state, or validation instead of `address(0)` mental models. | Mentions OpenZeppelin Stellar modules for fungible, non-fungible, RWA/ERC-3643, allowlist/blocklist, pausable, access control, and upgradeability. | Mentions gas/resource differences: simulate to estimate resources/fees; avoid EVM gas-refund assumptions.
Golden cites: Official EVM migration docs and authorization docs. | Official SAC/token overview or SEP-41 docs for token mapping. | OpenZeppelin Stellar docs or repository when citing OZ modules.

Both version numbers are volatile; grade the Draft and pre-alpha status, not one release number. Auth—not syntax—is the top scored footgun.
